case_studies.title: Tool-Making and Self-Evolving LLM Agents in Low-Latency Systems
case_studies.abstract: Production LLM agents often waste latency and reliability by regenerating code for the same procedural steps on every request. We replace this inference-time coding loop with an agentic tool-making pipeline that compiles repeated SOP steps into validated, versioned tools before deployment. The tool-maker grounds synthesis in the live environment as it collects execution traces, observes backend schemas and values, generates candidate tools, and repairs them against labeled cases. At runtime, the production agent calls these tools directly and falls back to code generation only when needed. We
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of latency and reliability in production LLM agents by replacing the inference-time coding loop with a tool-making pipeline. The researchers built a pipeline that compiles repeated procedural steps into validated tools before deployment. The result is improved latency and reliability in low-latency systems.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage low-latency systems with LLM agents, here is what to do: review your current code generation process, consider implementing a tool-making pipeline to compile repeated steps into validated tools, and assess the potential impact on your system's latency and reliability.

This directly affects how IT engineers work by enabling the use of pre-compiled tools, reducing the need for code regeneration on every request. This has significant value within 90 days as it can be used to improve the performance and efficiency of LLM-powered applications. The concept of agentic systems and MLOps automation is highly relevant to IT infrastructure and software engineering. case_studies.title: TTHE: Test-Time Harness Evolution
case_studies.abstract: The behavior of an LLM agent is determined not only by the underlying model, but also by its harness: the executable program that constructs context, invokes tools, verifies intermediate results, and recovers from failures. Existing approaches optimize such harnesses before deployment, searching training or development data for a fixed agent workflow that is then frozen at test time. This limits adaptation when the test distribution, failure modes, or tool interactions differ from those seen during development. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited adaptation in Large Language Model (LLM) agents by optimizing the harness during evaluation, the authors built a system called TTHE, and the result allows for better performance in changing environments. The harness is the program that surrounds the LLM model and interacts with it, and optimizing it during evaluation can improve the overall performance of the agent. This is not directly relevant to general IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Multi-Agent Firewall Architecture for Privacy Protection of Sensitive Data in Interactions with Language Models
case_studies.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have become essential productivity tools, their integration into workflows without adequate safeguards creates significant risks. This paper proposes an open-source, privacy-focused, user-facing firewall designed to secure both web-based and programmatic LLM interactions. The architecture combines a browser extension and a proxy for total traffic interception across both HTTP(S) and WebSocket communications. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of protecting sensitive data when using Large Language Models by building a multi-agent firewall architecture, which resulted in a privacy-focused, open-source firewall for securing LLM interactions. The firewall combines a browser extension and a proxy to intercept traffic and prevent data leakage. This architecture is designed to secure both web-based and programmatic LLM interactions.

case_studies.title: BiSCo-LLM: Lookup-Free Binary Spherical Coding for Extreme Low-Bit Large Language Model Compression
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly constrained by memory capacity, weight bandwidth, and checkpoint storage during deployment. Existing low-bit compression methods mainly follow two directions. Scalar or group-wise quantization is simple and compatible with efficient low-precision kernels, but its representation capacity becomes limited when the target budget approaches 2 bits per weight. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of large language model compression by building a new method called BiSCo-LLM, which achieves extreme low-bit compression without using lookup tables. The result is a more efficient way to compress large language models, reducing memory usage and storage needs. This is relevant to IT work in cloud infrastructure where large language models are deployed.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure for large language models, here is what to do: review your current compression methods, consider implementing BiSCo-LLM for more efficient compression, and assess the potential cost savings from reduced storage and memory usage.

case_studies.title: Workflow as Knowledge: Semantic Persistence for LLM-Mediated Workflows
case_studies.abstract: Large language model (LLM) applications increasingly use explicit workflows for tool use, retrieval, branching, checkpointing, and human approval. Existing workflow systems already address many execution concerns. This paper proposes a Lisp-inspired but language-independent conceptual model: symbolic forms, object identity, and live-image thinking are used as explanatory lenses, not implementation commitments. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of managing complex workflows in large language model applications by creating a conceptual model that represents workflow definitions and instances as persistent knowledge objects. The authors built a language-independent model using symbolic forms and object identity. The result is a shared knowledge base that can improve workflow execution and management.

case_studies.title: Institutional Red-Teaming: Deployment Rules, Not Just Models, Causally Shape Multi-Agent AI Safety
case_studies.abstract: We introduce institutional red-teaming, an evaluation methodology for testing deployment rules in multi-agent AI: hold the agents, objectives, and task state fixed, vary only one rule, and attribute the resulting change in collective behavior to that rule. We instantiate the methodology in IABench-CA, a consequence-allocation benchmark spanning 228 contexts, five canonical rules, and seven model populations (33,924 games), with a normative cooperative reference and auto-labelled reasoning traces. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of ensuring safety in multi-agent AI systems by introducing a new methodology to test deployment rules. The researchers built a benchmark called IABench-CA to evaluate the impact of different deployment rules on collective behavior. The result shows that deployment rules can causally alter collective safety in these systems.

case_studies.title: SLORR: Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
case_studies.abstract: Low-rank factorization is widely used to compress neural networks, but modern models are often not naturally amenable to aggressive factorization without significant accuracy loss. Existing training-time low-rank regularizers can improve compressibility, but they often require SVDs of large weight matrices, modify the model architecture (introducing additional trainable parameters), or rely on stateful cached quantities. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of compressing neural networks without losing accuracy by introducing a new framework called SLORR, which builds a simple and efficient in-training low-rank regularization method. The result is a compressed model that preserves its original architecture and accuracy. This is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel method for neural network compression, but lacks direct IT infrastructure application. Possible interest in the field if an IT engineer has to deal with large neural networks

case_studies.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
case_studies.abstract: A national language model offers a linguistic community its own instrument for measuring what its citizens say and value. Portugal's AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter model for European Portuguese, appears competitive on agreement alone: asked to code the moral foundation of authority, it agrees with trained human coders to within six F1 points of open models eight to thirteen times its size. case_studies.summary: This research explores the validity of large language models as data annotators, specifically testing Portugal's AMALIA model on coding moral foundations of authority. The model showed competitive results, agreeing with human coders within six F1 points of larger models. However, the study highlights the difference between agreement and validity in theoretical constructs.

case_studies.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
case_studies.abstract: Recent work identified Super Weights, individual parameters whose removal degrades model performance by orders of magnitude. We show that this degradation due to pruning Super Weights does not universally apply to all LLMs. Furthermore, if these parameters are so important, Super Weight-aware training should be effective. We show the opposite. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of understanding how Super Weights affect the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs). case_studies.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based web search agents are transforming information seeking from simple factoid question answering into complex, deep-and-wide search and research-oriented tasks. A single ReAct-style agent is constrained by one long trajectory and limited context, making it difficult to handle depth and coverage simultaneously. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of deep-and-wide web search by building a recursive multi-agent system called WebSwarm, which improves search coverage and recursive depth.
